transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I am new to Excel. What is a worksheet, and how do sheet tabs help me move around a workbook?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: A workbook is the Excel file. Inside you have sheet tabs, each one is a worksheet. I can rename a tab by right-clicking it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If A1 has 10 and I copy a formula from B1 to B2, why might the cell reference change? What does $A$1 mean?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Every cell is identified by column letter and row number like B3. A range is A1:C4. A relative reference like =A2 changes when copied down. But $A$1 is absolute and stays fixed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Could you show me a small numbers example using SUM or AVERAGE, starting with the equals sign?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Formulas start with =. SUM adds numbers, AVERAGE gives the mean. =IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail") checks a condition. I use cell references instead of typing values.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: How would you show the same number as money, a percentage, or a date? Why does the number format matter?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Number formats change display, not the value. 0.25 as percentage shows 25%. Currency adds a symbol. I select the range first, then apply format and use wrap text.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: What makes an Excel table useful? Please explain headers, sorting, filtering, and a totals row.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: An Excel table has headers. Sorting rearranges complete rows. Filtering hides non-matching rows without deleting. A totals row can sum a column.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you. I have asked my five practice questions. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: A column chart compares categories. A line chart shows change over time. I select data range with labels, add a chart title and label axes.
